sop_modules.name: Exterior Fiber Cement Siding Protection & Equipment Setup
sop_modules.description: Deploy landscape/hardscape protection, mask fixtures, set up access equipment and spray rigs. Window/door protection is NOT this spec's responsibility — belongs in window/door specs (wood siding RC-001).

tasks.name: Landscape Protection Setup
tasks.description: Deploy tarps and plastic sheeting along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent to siding work area. Measured in linear feet along the foundation/siding line. Full cover for spray, edge tarps for brush/roll.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of plantings within spray drift zone. Secure tarps against wind.

tasks.name: Hardscape Protection Setup
tasks.description: Deploy drop cloths and plastic over walkways, patios, and driveways adjacent to siding.

quality_notes.all: Tape plastic to foundation at grade line. Extend coverage to drip/overspray zone.

tasks.name: Fixture and Utility Masking
tasks.description: Mask exterior light fixtures, house numbers, utility panels, hose bibs. Bag and tape HVAC units if adjacent.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of all fixtures and utility connections on working elevation.

tasks.name: Spray Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Set up ladders, scaffold, or lift per access_type. Configure airless sprayer, hoses, tips for fiber cement siding. Stage materials.

quality_notes.all: Verify tip size: 517 for lap/panel, 413 for shingle profile. Stage enough material for full elevation run.

tasks.name: Brush/Roll Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Set up ladders, scaffold, or lift per access_type. Stage brushes, rollers, trays, and materials.

quality_notes.all: Stage enough material for full elevation run.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Landscape/hardscape protection first → Fixture masking → Equipment setup last.

sop_modules.name: Fiber Cement Siding Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: NC fiber cement prep: low-pressure wash (NO power washing), scuff sand for adhesion, end-seal cut edges, caulk siding-to-trim joints, dust cleanup. Tasks activate based on substrate_state.

tasks.name: Low-Pressure Wash
tasks.description: Clean siding surface with garden hose and soft-to-medium bristle brush. Remove construction dust, dirt, and debris. HIGH-PRESSURE POWER WASHING IS PROHIBITED on fiber cement — strips paint, damages texture, forces water behind wall assembly.

quality_notes.QT3: Full low-pressure wash. Allow 24 hr dry time.
quality_notes.QT4: Full low-pressure wash with TSP solution. Allow 24-48 hr dry time.

tasks.name: Scuff Sand for Adhesion
tasks.description: Light scuff sand siding surface with 150-180 grit for mechanical adhesion profile. Required for factory-primed and factory-finished surfaces.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Full surface scuff sand — critical for bonding primer adhesion on oven-baked finish

quality_notes.QT3: Light scuff. Not removing material — creating tooth.
quality_notes.QT4: Full surface scuff. Uniform scratch pattern. Inspect for missed areas.

tasks.name: End-Seal Field-Cut Edges
tasks.description: Brush end-cut sealer on ALL field-cut edges. Cut edges expose cellulose fibers that absorb water via capillary action — the #1 failure mode for fiber cement (FM-001). Includes butt joints, miters, and field cuts.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Factory primer covers face but cut edges are bare
Factory finish covers face but cut edges remain unsealed
Assumed sealed during prior prime application

quality_notes.all: EVERY cut edge sealed. Non-negotiable for warranty and performance. Inspect all joints, miters, and field cuts.

tasks.name: Caulk Siding-to-Trim Joints
tasks.description: Apply exterior paintable caulk to all siding-to-trim joints. Do NOT caulk field butt joints on lap siding — creates moisture trap behind joint. Use flexible caulk (polyurethane or siliconized acrylic).

quality_notes.QT3: All siding-to-trim joints caulked. Smooth tool.
quality_notes.QT4: All joints caulked with consistent bead. Precision tool smooth. Inspect for uniformity.

tasks.name: Prep Dust Cleanup
tasks.description: Remove sanding dust and debris from all surfaces before coating. Tack cloth or compressed air.

quality_notes.all: All dust removed. Surface ready for primer application.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Low-pressure wash → Dry time (24-48 hr) → Scuff sand (factory-primed/factory-finished) → End-seal cut edges → Caulk siding-to-trim joints → Dust cleanup.

sop_modules.name: Fiber Cement Siding Field Prime Coat
sop_modules.description: Full field prime coat. Three substrate-driven primer paths: (1) acrylic primer for factory-primed, (2) alkali-resistant primer (Loxon) for bare FC, (3) bonding primer for factory-finished (ColorPlus). Skipped entirely for SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD.

tasks.name: Prime Coat — Spray Application
tasks.description: Apply full prime coat by airless spray. Even, consistent mil thickness across all siding field. Primer product determined by substrate state (acrylic / alkali-resistant / bonding).

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays or thin spots.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build. Inspect for coverage.
quality_notes.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Inspect under raking light at 3 ft.

tasks.name: Prime Coat — Brush/Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply full prime coat by brush and roller. Brush for edges and transitions, roller for open field. Primer product determined by substrate state.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage. Work primer into surface. No holidays. Maintain wet edge.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Single prime coat. Method by application_method dimension. Substrate state determines primer product. Module SKIPPED entirely when substrate_state = SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD.

sop_modules.name: Fiber Cement Siding Finish Coat 1
sop_modules.description: First finish coat. Spray application is primary — NO back-rolling on fiber cement (introduces unwanted stipple/orange peel on factory-smooth surface). Brush/roll is fallback method only.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray Application
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by airless spray. NO back-rolling — spray only for factory-smooth fiber cement surface. Consistent mil build, uniform coverage.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. No drips or holidays.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build. No visible spray pattern at 6 ft.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Brush/Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by brush and roller. Fallback method for small projects <750 SF, occupied adjacent areas, or high wind conditions.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage. Consistent roller texture. Maintain wet edge to lap line.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: First finish coat. Spray is primary method. No back-rolling on fiber cement. Allow recoat time per product TDS before interstage/coat 2. QT2 may stop here (single finish coat).

sop_modules.name: Fiber Cement Siding Interstage Inspection
sop_modules.description: Inspect first finish coat, touch up defects. Light sand at QT4 only. Module skipped for QT2 single-coat systems.

tasks.name: Interstage Inspection
tasks.description: Inspect first finish coat for holidays, runs, sags, and coverage defects.

quality_notes.QT3: Quick scan for obvious defects — runs, sags, holidays.
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic inspection at 6 ft viewing distance. Mark all visible defects.

tasks.name: Interstage Light Sand
tasks.description: Light sand between finish coats with 220 grit for mechanical adhesion. QT4 only — not required at QT3 per research.json.

quality_notes.QT4: Light scuff sand. Remove nibs and defects. Uniform scratch pattern.

tasks.name: Interstage Touch-Up
tasks.description: Repair defects found during interstage inspection. Brush touch-up.

quality_notes.QT4: Fix all defects found during inspection. Blend repairs.

tasks.name: Intercoat Dust Removal
tasks.description: Remove sanding dust before second coat. Tack cloth or compressed air.

quality_notes.all: All sanding dust removed before second finish coat.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect → Sand (QT4 only) → Touch up → Dust removal → Coat 2. Module skipped for QT2 single-coat systems.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs after finish coat 1, before finish coat 2. Skipped for QT2 single-coat.

sop_modules.name: Fiber Cement Siding Finish Coat 2
sop_modules.description: Second (final) finish coat. Required at QT3 and QT4. Skipped at QT2 (single coat). Spray only — no back-rolling.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray Application
tasks.description: Apply second (final) finish coat by airless spray. Critical for appearance and film build. NO back-rolling.

quality_notes.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. Final appearance coat.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Brush/Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply second finish coat by brush and roller. Fallback method.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage. No brush marks. Maintain wet edge to lap line. Final coat.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Second and final finish coat. Skipped at QT2.

sop_modules.name: Fiber Cement Siding Final Inspection
sop_modules.description: Final walkthrough of completed siding finish. Touch up defects found.

tasks.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
tasks.description: Walk all elevations and inspect finished siding for coverage, consistency, and defects.

quality_notes.QT2: Ground-level walkthrough. Quick scan for misses.
quality_notes.QT3: Ground-level walkthrough at 6-10 ft viewing distance.
quality_notes.QT4: Ground-level with binoculars for upper elevations. 6 ft viewing standard.

tasks.name: Final Touch-Up
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection.

quality_notes.QT4: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly at 3 ft standard.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect all elevations → Touch up → Sign off.

sop_modules.name: Fiber Cement Siding Cleanup & Protection Teardown
sop_modules.description: Remove all protection materials, clean equipment, restore site.

tasks.name: Protection Material Removal
tasks.description: Remove all masking tape, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, fixture bags, HVAC covers.

quality_notes.all: Check for tape residue. Remove all protection materials completely.

tasks.name: Clean Equipment
tasks.description: Flush airless sprayer, clean tips and filters, coil hoses. Clean brushes and rollers if used.

quality_notes.all: Full flush cycle for sprayer. Tips and filters cleaned and stored.

tasks.name: Site Debris Cleanup
tasks.description: Collect all debris — sandpaper, caulk tubes, tape, sealer containers, paint cans. Leave site clean.

quality_notes.all: Site restored to pre-work condition. All materials and debris removed.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Protection teardown → Equipment cleaning → Site cleanup.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 2 Finish Coats
round_configurations.description: Standard NC sequence: 1 field prime + 2 finish coats. Required at QT3/QT4.
round_configurations.notes: James Hardie warranty requires 2 topcoats. Field prime over factory prime is mandatory.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 1 Finish Coat (Economy)
round_configurations.description: Economy QT2 sequence: 1 field prime + 1 finish coat.
round_configurations.notes: QT2 economy tier. Single finish coat acceptable on primed surfaces per Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine §4.5.

round_configurations.name: 2 Finish Coats Only (Field-Primed)
round_configurations.description: Skip prime, direct to 2 finish coats. For SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD only.
round_configurations.notes: Field prime already applied in prior mobilization.

round_configurations.name: 1 Finish Coat Only (Economy, Field-Primed)
round_configurations.description: Economy single finish coat on field-primed surface.
round_configurations.notes: QT2 economy on already-primed surface. Minimum viable scope.

assumptions.value: Finish coats spray-only on fiber cement — no back-rolling
assumptions.note: Explicit doctrine: 'Fiber cement (Hardiplank): Back-rolling introduces unwanted stipple/orange peel — spray-only for factory-smooth finish.'

assumptions.value: Low-pressure wash (garden hose + soft brush) only — power washing prohibited
assumptions.note: Explicit doctrine: power washing strips paint, damages texture, forces water behind wall assembly.

assumptions.value: End-cut edge sealing is non-negotiable for all field-cut fiber cement edges
assumptions.note: Edge wicking (FM-001) is the #1 failure mode for fiber cement.
